prompt: A concave mirror produces three times magnified real image of an object placed at 10 cm in front of it. Where is the image located?
gold_answer: -30 cm
gold_citations: NCERT Class 10 Science, Light - Reflection and Refraction, Section 9.2.4 Mirror Formula and Magnification

sample_answers.text: The image is 30 cm in front of the mirror, so v = -30 cm.
v = +30 cm, behind the mirror.

prompt: State the two laws of reflection of light.
gold_answer: 1. The angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection. 2. The incident ray, the normal to the mirror at the point of incidence, and the reflected ray all lie in the same plane.
gold_citations: NCERT Class 10 Science, Light - Reflection and Refraction, Section 9.1 Reflection of Light

sample_answers.text: Angle of incidence equals angle of reflection, and the incident ray, normal and reflected ray lie in one plane.
The angle of incidence equals the angle the reflected ray makes with the mirror surface.

prompt: If a potential difference of 12 V across an electric component results in a current of 2.5 A, calculate the resistance.
gold_answer: 4.8 ohms
gold_citations: NCERT Class 10 Science, Electricity, Section 11.4 Ohm's Law

sample_answers.text: R = V x I = 30 ohm.

prompt: In a spherical-mirror diagram, where is the centre of curvature C located for a concave mirror and for a convex mirror, and how is the principal axis defined?
gold_answer: For a concave mirror, C lies in front of the mirror; for a convex mirror, C lies behind it. The principal axis is the straight line through the pole P and centre of curvature C, and it is normal to the mirror at P.
gold_citations: NCERT Class 10 Science, Light - Reflection and Refraction, Section 9.2 Spherical Mirrors

sample_answers.text: C is in front of a concave mirror and behind a convex one; the principal axis passes through P and C, normal to the mirror at P.
C and F are the same point, on the mirror surface.

prompt: An object is placed between C and F of a concave mirror. Using the standard ray-diagram rules, state the position, relative size, orientation, and nature of the image.
gold_answer: The image forms beyond C; it is enlarged, inverted, and real.
gold_citations: NCERT Class 10 Science, Light - Reflection and Refraction, Section 9.2.1 Image Formation by Spherical Mirrors, Table 9.1
NCERT Class 10 Science, Light - Reflection and Refraction, Section 9.2.2 Representation of Images Formed by Spherical Mirrors Using Ray Diagrams

sample_answers.text: Beyond C; the image is real, inverted and enlarged.
Between F and P; the image is virtual and erect.

prompt: A convex mirror is used as a rear-view mirror. For an object at a finite distance in front of it, where is the image formed and what are its nature, orientation, and relative size?
gold_answer: The image forms behind the mirror between P and F; it is virtual, erect, and diminished.
gold_citations: NCERT Class 10 Science, Light - Reflection and Refraction, Section 9.2.2, Image formation by a Convex Mirror, Table 9.2
NCERT Class 10 Science, Light - Reflection and Refraction, Uses of convex mirrors

sample_answers.text: Behind the mirror between P and F; virtual, erect and diminished.
In front of the mirror; real, inverted and enlarged.

prompt: A ray of light travels obliquely from air into glass. In which direction does it bend relative to the normal, and what change in the speed of light accompanies this bending?
gold_answer: It bends towards the normal and its speed decreases on entering the optically denser glass.
gold_citations: NCERT Class 10 Science, Light - Reflection and Refraction, Section 9.3.1 Refraction through a Rectangular Glass Slab
NCERT Class 10 Science, Light - Reflection and Refraction, Section 9.3.2 The Refractive Index

sample_answers.text: It bends towards the normal and slows down in the denser glass.
It bends away from the normal and speeds up.

prompt: The refractive index of a glass medium is 1.50. Taking the speed of light in vacuum as 3.0 × 10^8 m/s, calculate the speed of light in the glass.
gold_citations: NCERT Class 10 Science, Light - Reflection and Refraction, Section 9.3.2 The Refractive Index

prompt: An object is placed at 2F1 of a convex lens. According to the ray diagram, where is the image formed and what are its size, orientation, and nature?
gold_answer: The image forms at 2F2; it is the same size as the object, inverted, and real.
gold_citations: NCERT Class 10 Science, Light - Reflection and Refraction, Section 9.3.4 Image Formation by Lenses, Table 9.4
NCERT Class 10 Science, Light - Reflection and Refraction, Section 9.3.5 Image Formation in Lenses Using Ray Diagrams

sample_answers.text: At 2F2; same size, inverted and real.
Beyond 2F2; enlarged and virtual.

prompt: In the human eye, state the main roles of the cornea, iris and pupil, crystalline lens, and retina in forming and detecting an image.
gold_answer: Most refraction occurs at the cornea; the iris controls pupil size and therefore the amount of light entering; the crystalline lens fine-tunes focal length to focus light; the retina receives the real inverted image and its light-sensitive cells generate signals sent to the brain.
gold_citations: NCERT Class 10 Science, Human Eye and the Colourful World, Section 10.1 The Human Eye
chapter: Human Eye and the Colourful World

sample_answers.text: The cornea does most of the refraction, the iris sets the pupil size to control light, the lens fine-tunes focus, and the retina detects the image.
The pupil focuses the light and the cornea detects the image.

prompt: When a normal eye shifts focus from a distant object to a nearby object, how do the ciliary muscles, curvature of the eye lens, and focal length change?
gold_answer: The ciliary muscles contract, the lens becomes thicker with greater curvature, and its focal length decreases.
gold_citations: NCERT Class 10 Science, Human Eye and the Colourful World, Section 10.1.1 Power of Accommodation
chapter: Human Eye and the Colourful World

sample_answers.text: The ciliary muscles contract, the lens gets thicker and more curved, and its focal length decreases.
The retina moves backwards while the lens stays the same.

prompt: A student can read a nearby book clearly but cannot see the classroom blackboard distinctly from the back row. Where would the image of a distant object tend to form in this eye, and what type of lens corrects the defect?
gold_answer: The image of a distant object forms in front of the retina; a concave lens of suitable power corrects the defect.
gold_citations: NCERT Class 10 Science, Human Eye and the Colourful World, Section 10.2 Defects of Vision and Their Correction, Myopia subsection
chapter: Human Eye and the Colourful World

sample_answers.text: The image forms in front of the retina; a concave lens corrects it.
The image forms behind the retina; a convex lens corrects it.

prompt: A person sees distant objects clearly but must hold a book much farther than 25 cm to read comfortably. Where would light from a nearby object tend to focus, and what type of corrective lens is used?
gold_answer: The light would tend to focus behind the retina; a convex lens of suitable power is used for correction.
gold_citations: NCERT Class 10 Science, Human Eye and the Colourful World, Section 10.2 Defects of Vision and Their Correction, Hypermetropia subsection
chapter: Human Eye and the Colourful World

sample_answers.text: The light would focus behind the retina; a convex lens is used.
It focuses in front of the retina; a concave lens is used.

prompt: Why does the near point often recede with age in presbyopia?
gold_answer: With ageing, the ciliary muscles weaken and the eye lens becomes less flexible, reducing the power of accommodation and making nearby objects harder to focus clearly.
gold_citations: NCERT Class 10 Science, Human Eye and the Colourful World, Section 10.2 Defects of Vision and Their Correction, Presbyopia subsection
chapter: Human Eye and the Colourful World

sample_answers.text: The ciliary muscles weaken and the lens loses flexibility, reducing accommodation.
Because the eyeball becomes too long with age.

prompt: In a ray diagram for a triangular glass prism, how does a ray bend at the air-to-glass face and at the glass-to-air face, and why is the final emergent ray generally not parallel to the incident ray?
gold_answer: It bends towards the normal on entering glass and away from the normal on leaving glass. The prism faces are inclined to each other, so these two refractions produce a net angular deviation rather than restoring the original direction.
gold_citations: NCERT Class 10 Science, Human Eye and the Colourful World, Section 10.3 Refraction of Light Through a Prism
chapter: Human Eye and the Colourful World

sample_answers.text: Towards the normal on entering, away on leaving; the faces are inclined, so there is a net deviation.
It bends equally and oppositely, so the emergent ray stays parallel to the incident ray.

prompt: When white light passes through a glass prism, which visible colour is deviated least and which is deviated most? What does this difference produce?
gold_answer: Red is deviated least and violet most; the different deviations separate white light into its spectrum of component colours.
gold_citations: NCERT Class 10 Science, Human Eye and the Colourful World, Section 10.4 Dispersion of White Light by a Glass Prism
chapter: Human Eye and the Colourful World

sample_answers.text: Red least, violet most; this separates white light into a spectrum.
Violet least and red most; the prism adds colours to the light.

prompt: Why are danger signal lights commonly red rather than blue, especially when they must be seen through fog or smoke?
gold_answer: Red light is scattered the least by fog or smoke, so it can remain visible in the same colour over a greater distance than shorter-wavelength light such as blue.
gold_citations: NCERT Class 10 Science, Human Eye and the Colourful World, Section 10.6.2 Why is the colour of the clear Sky Blue?
chapter: Human Eye and the Colourful World

sample_answers.text: Red is scattered least by fog or smoke, so it is seen from farther away.
Red light travels faster than blue light.

prompt: In a metallic wire connected in a closed circuit, electrons drift from the negative terminal toward the positive terminal. In which direction is conventional electric current taken?
gold_answer: Conventional current is taken in the opposite direction to electron flow, from the positive terminal toward the negative terminal through the external circuit.
gold_citations: NCERT Class 10 Science, Electricity, Section 11.1 Electric Current and Circuit

sample_answers.text: Opposite to electron flow: from positive to negative through the external circuit.
In the same direction as the electrons, from negative to positive.

prompt: In a circuit diagram, how should a voltmeter be connected to measure the potential difference across a resistor?
gold_answer: The voltmeter is connected in parallel across the two ends of the resistor.
gold_citations: NCERT Class 10 Science, Electricity, Section 11.2 Electric Potential and Potential Difference

sample_answers.text: In parallel, across the two ends of the resistor.
In series with the resistor.

prompt: Two wires are made of the same material and have the same length, but one has twice the cross-sectional area of the other. How do their resistances compare?
gold_answer: Since R = rho l/A, doubling the cross-sectional area halves the resistance; the thicker wire has half the resistance of the thinner wire.
gold_citations: NCERT Class 10 Science, Electricity, Section 11.5 Factors on which the Resistance of a Conductor Depends

sample_answers.text: The thicker wire has half the resistance, since R = rho l/A.
The thicker wire has twice the resistance.

prompt: A 20 ohm lamp and a 4 ohm resistor are connected in series to a 6 V battery. Find the equivalent resistance and the current through the circuit.
gold_answer: Equivalent resistance = 24 ohms; current = 0.25 A.
gold_citations: NCERT Class 10 Science, Electricity, Section 11.6.1 Resistors in Series, Example 11.7

prompt: Three resistors of 5 ohms, 10 ohms, and 30 ohms are connected in parallel across a 12 V battery. Find the equivalent resistance and the total current drawn from the battery.
gold_answer: Equivalent resistance = 3 ohms; total current = 4 A.
gold_citations: NCERT Class 10 Science, Electricity, Section 11.6.2 Resistors in Parallel, Example 11.8

prompt: A student says that adding another resistor always increases the equivalent resistance of a circuit. Explain why this statement is true for a series addition but not for adding a new parallel branch.
gold_answer: In series, resistances add directly, so the equivalent resistance increases. In parallel, reciprocals add, providing an additional path for current, so the equivalent resistance decreases and is less than the smallest branch resistance.
gold_citations: NCERT Class 10 Science, Electricity, Section 11.6.1 Resistors in Series
NCERT Class 10 Science, Electricity, Section 11.6.2 Resistors in Parallel

sample_answers.text: Series resistances add, so R increases; a new parallel branch adds a path, so R decreases below the smallest branch.
Adding any resistor always increases the total resistance.

prompt: An electric iron of resistance 20 ohms carries a current of 5 A for 30 s. Calculate the heat produced.
gold_citations: NCERT Class 10 Science, Electricity, Section 11.7 Heating Effect of Electric Current, Joule's law of heating
